To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the persistent current of Luttingering liquid in one-dimensional rings with a weak link is described by the power law I(L) $\propto L^{1+\alpha}$ for large L and that the power $\alpha$, which depends only on the e-e interaction, is given by the formula $\alpha$ = {(1 + $2 \alpha_{R G}$)}1/2 - 1 for small-range e-e interaction.

the power law $J \propto L^{1-\alpha}$ of the persistent current is valid already for a small number of electrons, and that this power law holds for a broad range of e-e interactions, but only if the range $d$ of V(x-x') is small enough.
the Luttinger-liquid behavior is observed in our numerical results for a single weak link with the range of V(r) approaching zero and the interaction parameter $\alpha_{Rg}$ larger than zero.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Luttinger-liquid behaviour in one dimension.
the many-body problem of correlated electrons in a ring.
the persistent current of a Luttinger liquid with a continuous model and a short range e-e interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Luttinger-liquid power law $I(L) \propto L^{1-\alpha}$ is a general feature of the one-dimensional ring with the weak link and the short-range e-e interaction, however, the exponent $\alpha$ depends on the range of V(q), i.e., it depends on the details of the model.

the persistent current of Luttinging liquid in the continuous model is described by the power law $L^{-1-\alpha_{RG}}$ for small range of V(x-x'), by the exponential law for large range of V(x), and by the Hartree-Fork law for intermediate range of V(x).

the power-law behaviour of the persistent current in the Luttinger-liquid regime is a universal property of the continuous model, which holds for any range of the e-e interaction, but only if the range is small enough.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the power law I(L) $\propto L^{-\alpha}$, where $\alpha$ depends solely on the e-e interaction, is valid for the continuous model of the one-dimensional ring with one weak link, if the range of e-e interaction is small enough, and if the number of electrons in the ring is large enough.

the Luttinger-liquid theory is valid for continuous model with short-range e-e interaction, and that the Hartree-Foc approximation is a good approximation to the power-law I(L) only if the range d of V(x -x') is small enough.
the power law $L^{-1-\alpha_{RG}}$ holds in the continuous one-dimensional ring only if the range $d$ is small.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Luttinger-liquid behavior of the persistent current is not restricted to the lattice model but is a universal property of correlated electrons in a ring with a weak link.
the Luttinger-liquid behaviour is not an artefact of the lattice model.
, the persistent current in one-dimensional rings with weak links can be studied in a continuous model by the advanced CI method, and the DMC method in the fixed-phase approximation.
